inspiration.observed_pattern: Grouped reports use HAVING COUNT(...) to retain only groups whose membership meets a minimum threshold, including a joined category-level count.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an original department staffing report with a LEFT JOIN and an active-employee predicate in the join condition. HAVING COUNT(employee_id) >= 2 keeps departments with at least two active employees, including a qualifying department whose SUM of nullable bonus points remains NULL.

fixture_notes: Department 10 has three active employees and a bonus total of 25; department 20 has only one active employee because its second employee is inactive and is excluded by the JOIN predicate; department 30 has no employees and is filtered out by HAVING; department 40 has two active employees with NULL bonuses and remains because HAVING counts rows independently of SUM.
determinism_notes: Department and employee IDs are fixed; the grouped report is ordered by the unique department ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE departments (department_id INT PRIMARY KEY, department_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE employees (employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY, department_id INT NOT NULL, employee_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, active TINYINT NOT NULL, bonus_points INT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT d.department_id, d.department_name, COUNT(e.employee_id) AS active_employee_count, SUM(e.bonus_points) AS total_bonus_points FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.department_id AND e.active = 1 GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name HAVING COUNT(e.employee_id) >= 2 ORDER BY d.department_id

checks.sql: SELECT department_id, department_name FROM departments ORDER BY department_id
SELECT employee_id, department_id, employee_name, active, bonus_points FROM employees ORDER BY employee_id
